variants.title: Choose the durable owner
variants.context: A source of truth is the authoritative record used to resolve what is correct.
variants.prompt: An application restarts after confirming an order. Where must the confirmed order survive?
options: In durable storage that survives restart.
Only in the process’s in-memory cache.
Only in a log buffer that has not been persisted.
variants.hint: Distinguish authoritative data from a derived or lagging copy.
variants.explanation: A local process can disappear; confirmed business facts need durable storage.
optionFeedback: A local process can disappear; confirmed business facts need durable storage.

variants.explanation: Replica lag matters when a request requires the latest acknowledged state.

variants.title: Estimate raw storage
variants.context: A storage estimate multiplies record count by average bytes per record. Ignore indexes, replicas, and overhead in this raw-data exercise.
variants.prompt: There are 100000 records averaging 200 bytes each. What is raw storage in decimal MB?
variants.hint: Compute bytes first, then divide by one million.

mistakes.feedback: That is mebibytes. Dividing by 1,048,576 gives the binary unit, not decimal MB.
That is kilobytes. You divided by 1,000 rather than by 1,000,000.

variants.title: Choose a lookup key
variants.context: An index is an additional structure that helps find records by selected fields; it takes storage and write work.
variants.prompt: Most reads look up a link by short_code. What field is the first index candidate?
options: An index on creation time for recent links.
An index on the short_code column.
An index on the destination URL field.
variants.hint: Connect the query or invariant to a database structure.
variants.explanation: Index the field that serves the important access pattern.
optionFeedback: Reads do not filter by creation time, so that index adds write cost for nothing.
Index the field that serves the important access pattern.
No query filters by destination, so a destination index is never read.
